facts.text: The court’s arrival page directs visitors to enter from Main Street. It does not identify a step-free doorway or establish a continuous route from parking.
facts.quote: Enter Courthouse from Main Street.

facts.text: The court says the building opens at 8 a.m. and security-checkpoint lines are much longer from 8:30 to 9:30 a.m. Allow time for screening; a shorter wait outside that hour is not guaranteed.
facts.quote: Between the hour of 8:30 A.M. to 9:30 A.M. patrons will encounter much longer lines and wait times. Please make sure to take this into consideration when determining your arrival time. Note: Courthouse will open daily at 8:00 A.M.

facts.text: Everyone entering the Courthouse or Justice Center must pass security screening and metal detectors. The page says deputies will not store items they consider dangerous or issue claim tickets for them; those items must be left in the visitor’s car. Confirm screening arrangements for medical equipment with the court.
facts.quote: All persons entering the Courthouse and Justice Center are required to pass security screenings and metal detectors **Deputy Sheriff's will no longer be issuing claim tickets for items deemed by them to be dangerous items. This list includes, but is not limited to: pocket knives, scissors, mace, or any other weapon. If you feel you have a dangerous item in your possession you will need to leave it in your car. The Sheriff will not let you in the building with these items.**

facts.text: For people serving as jurors, the Jury Commission lists a quiet area in Room 468. This is a juror amenity, not a confirmed quiet room for every courthouse visitor. Its physical layout and entry arrangements are not described.
facts.quote: Jurors Quiet Area (Room 468)

facts.text: The juror amenities list includes private bathrooms, a private room for nursing mothers, drinking water, and access to a refrigerator, freezer and microwave. Toilet layouts, changing equipment and access for non-jurors are not established.
facts.quote: Private Bathrooms Jurors Quiet Area (Room 468) Private Room for Nursing Mothers Landline Telephone Access Free Coffee, Tea, and Water Refrigerator, Freezer, and Microwave Access

facts.text: The Jury Commission warns that its office can run hot or cold and recommends bringing a jacket for colder temperatures. This describes the jury office, not temperature control throughout the building.
facts.quote: Because the Courthouse is an older building the Jury Commission Office tends to run either hot or cold. We are constantly in communication with the Building Manager to make our space as comfortable as possible, however, it is difficult to find a comfortable temperature. With that in mind it is our recommendation that you come prepared with a jacket for colder temperatures.

facts.text: The juror FAQ permits a packed lunch and a drinking container with a lid. It warns that metal cutlery may be confiscated at security; the jury office provides plastic cutlery and plates. Confirm arrangements separately if attending for another purpose.
facts.quote: You are more than welcome to pack your lunch and any drinking vessel that you prefer so long as it has a lid. For your convenience the Jury Commission Office is equipped with a refrigerator, freezer, and 2 microwaves. Do not bring metal cutlery as it is possible it could be confiscated at the security checkpoint upon arrival. We have plastic cutlery and plates available here for you to use.

facts.text: The court lists Alms & Doepke Parkhaus at 1123 Sycamore Street as credit-card-only. Its instructions use a phone camera to open a QR payment link near the elevator shafts or bottom of the stairwell, then pay in a web browser without downloading an app. Jurors who cannot obtain the published discount are directed to the Jury Commission office for help; an alternative payment method is not established.
facts.quote: The Alms & Doepke Parkhaus Garage (credit card only) is located at 1123 Sycamore Street at the corner of Reading Road. It is behind the Alms & Doepke Building (Department of Job and Family Services), across central Parkway from the Courthouse and one city block from the County Administration Building. To pay for your parking at this garage you will pay online after you have arrived. There is a QR Code near all the elevator shafts and again at the bottom of the stairwell in the garage. Do not take a picture of the QR Code, but rather hover over the QR Code using the camera on your phone and a link to their website will appear. Do not download the app. Instead please pay directly through the Web Browser. With the Jury Duty Promo Code you will pay a rate of $7.35 for your parking. Please contact the Jury Commission (513-946-5879: hit "0" on your dialpad after 8:00 a.m.) to obtain the promo code. If you can not figure out how to obtain the $7.35 juror rate please do not pay at the garage, but rather come to the Jury Commission Office in the Courthouse and we can help you here.

facts.text: The court’s Court and Walnut garage instructions give the vehicle entrance as Central Parkway, at 119 Central Parkway E, and describe credit-card-only payment. For juror validation, collect a chaser ticket from the Jury Commission and use it after the original ticket at the vehicle exit gate, not at a ground-floor walk-up kiosk. These are parking procedures, not a verified step-free walk to the courthouse.
facts.quote: Court and Walnut Garage (3CDC) (credit card only) is located at 119 Central Parkway E. It is located above the new Kroger development on Court and Walnut Streets. You must enter the garage from Central Parkway. You will receive a parking slip when you arrive at the garage gate. While you are in the Courthouse you will come to one of the Jury Commission Offices to obtain a chaser ticket that you will use when you exit the garage. The original ticket will go in first and our chaser ticket will go in second. After that you will be asked to pay a rate of $6.00. Do not attempt to use our chaser ticket at either of the walk up kiosks on the ground floor of the building. Instead you will return immediately to your car and you will pay for your parking at the exit gate.

facts.text: The court lists public touchscreen case-schedule kiosks at either end of the main entrance and outside Room 255. For Municipal Court hearing-location information by phone, it lists the Assignment Commissioner at 513-946-6250, weekdays 8 a.m.–4 p.m. Kiosk reach, screen-reader support and an assisted-use procedure are not described.
facts.quote: Call the Municipal Court Assignment Commissioner's office at (513) 946-6250, between 8:00 AM and 4:00 PM, weekdays. Visit the Assignment Commissioner's office in room 117 of the Justice Center, 1000 Sycamore, St., Cincinnati, Ohio or room 255 of the courthouse, 1000 Main St., between 8:00 AM and 4:00 PM, weekdays. Call the Clerk of Courts office at (513) 946-6010, 24 hours a day, every day of the year. See also APPEARING IN COURT . Civil Cases Civil cases are cases such as evictions and suits for money. If you have an attorney, be sure you to check with your attorney about where you should appear. If you need to call the courthouse, it is important that you look at the papers you have relating to your case before you call. If you have a case number, please have it ready if you need to call about a case. Information on civil cases can be obtained from the following sources: Look-Up/Confirm Criminal & Civil Cases Scheduled Next 7 Days Kiosk Computer Lists for All Courts Call the Municipal Court Clerk's office at (513) 946-5700, between 8:00 AM and 4:00 PM, weekdays. Visit the Municipal Court Clerk's office in room 115 of the courthouse, 1000 Main St., between 8:00 AM and 4:00 PM, weekdays. See also APPEARING IN COURT . Kiosk Computer Lists for All Courts These public, touch screen computers allow access to the criminal and civil case schedules for the next seven days for the Municipal and Common Pleas courts in Hamilton County, except the Juvenile Court. (See Look-Up/Confirm Criminal & Civil Cases Scheduled Next 7 Days .) In addition to other locations, there are kiosks computers at either end of the main entrance of the courthouse and outside of room 255.

facts.text: Court Administration lists Common Pleas information at 513-946-5801 and Municipal Court information at 513-946-5200. Contact the relevant court before travelling to ask about entrance, screening, seating and communication arrangements; this page does not describe a specific accommodation-request procedure.
facts.quote: Common Pleas Court Administrative Offices Information Phone: 513-946-5801 Fax: 513-946-5808 Municipal Court Information Phone: 513-946-5200

facts.text: The Clerk’s Help Center General Division is in Room 113 at 1000 Main Street. Its page lists walk-in hours Monday–Thursday 8 a.m.–3:30 p.m. and Friday 8 a.m.–3 p.m., with a daily 12:45–1:45 p.m. closure. Call 513-946-5650 before travelling; these are Help Center hours, not hours for every courthouse office.
facts.quote: Location of Hamilton County Clerk of Courts Help Center - General Division: Hamilton County Courthouse 1000 Main Street, Room 113 Cincinnati, OH 45202 Hours of Clerk of Courts Help Center - General Division open for walk-in visits: Monday-Thursday: 8:00 a.m. - 3:30 p.m. Friday: 8:00 a.m. - 3:00 p.m. Closed Daily From 12:45-1:45 p.m. Call the Clerk of Courts Help Center: General Division: 513-946-5650
facts.authority: Clerk/University partnership described on own page and linked from Clerk official self-help-resources page

facts.text: The district FAQ says it does not offer regular curbside pickup and directs customers to drive-through service at Erlanger, Covington and Independence. Confirm temporary pickup arrangements with the branch if its drive-through is closed.
facts.quote: At this time KCPL does not offer curbside service. Feel free to use our drive-thru at Covington, Erlanger and Independence

facts.text: The district does not check out or accept returns of telescopes through the drive-through; those transactions require going inside the branch.
facts.quote: At this time we are unable to check out or accept returns of our telescopes through the drive-thru. You must come inside the branch.

facts.text: An expired library card can be renewed by calling 859-962-4000 or emailing weblib@kentonlibrary.org, with current address verification. In-person renewal is also offered. This can avoid a separate trip to renew the card.
facts.quote: If your card has expired you may call the library at 859-962-4000 or email weblib@kentonlibrary.org and ask for your card to be renewed. Please verify your current address when renewing. You may also renew in person at any location.
